This NDA was presented before the Endocrinology and Metabolism Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on April 2, 2009.

recommendation.text: No single up/down approval vote; the panel voted on four questions. On cardiovascular safety (Q1) the panel voted 8 Yes / 5 No that CV risk was acceptably ruled out. On whether the animal thyroid C-cell tumor findings were shown not relevant to humans (Q2) it voted 1 Yes / 12 No. On whether the C-cell tumor data permit marketing (Q3) it split 6 Yes / 6 No / 1 Abstain. On whether the papillary thyroid cancer data permit marketing (Q4) it voted 12 Yes / 0 No / 1 Abstain.

quote.quote: With regard to Question 3, six panel members voted "yes", six voted "no" and one abstained.

linkages.concern: The committee was not persuaded that the rodent thyroid C-cell (medullary thyroid carcinoma) tumor findings were irrelevant to humans; those voting against marketing stated that the human risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma with liraglutide is unknown.
linkages.change: The professional labeling was approved with a boxed warning describing the nonclinical C-cell tumor finding and its potential clinical risk.

concern_quote.quote: Those voting "no" stated that the human risk of medullary thyroid carcinoma with liraglutide is unknown, that there are alternative anti-diabetic medications available, and that it was unclear whether liraglutide offers unique benefits in the treatment armamentarium for type 2 diabetes.

summary: An EMDAC meeting was held April 2, 2009, dominated by the rodent thyroid C-cell (medullary thyroid carcinoma) tumor signal and by cardiovascular safety. The panel voted 1-12 that human irrelevance of the C-cell findings was not demonstrated and split 6-6-1 on whether those data permit marketing, while favoring the CV data (8-5) and the papillary-cancer data (12-0). Reflecting these concerns, Victoza was approved with a boxed warning and contraindication for the C-cell/MTC risk, a REMS (Medication Guide plus Communication Plan), and postmarketing requirements including an MTC case-series registry and a large cardiovascular outcomes trial; the verbatim AC transcript is not in paperclip, so these facts are drawn from the FDA review documents' account.
